title: Vacant or unknown adjoining site: cone from an outdoor active habitable space within the lot (6 m)
text: For development adjoining a vacant or unknown site. C3.9.5 Where an adjoining property is vacant residential zoned land, or when the location of a major opening or an active habitable space is unknown, all sources of overlooking are oriented, offset or set back in accordance with Table 3.9a so that the cone of vision does not extend beyond the lot boundaries (refer Figure 3.9h). Table 3.9a: Outdoor active habitable space: 6m. C3.9.6 Notwithstanding C3.9.5 where the cone of vision extends beyond a lot boundary behind the street setback on an adjoining property, the source of overlooking is designed to restrict the view in the direction of the adjoining property through one or more of the following: i. incorporate a permanent, fixed vertical or horizontal building element such as a fin or window hood (refer Figure 3.9i); ii. have permanent, obscure glazing in any part of the window below 1.6m above floor level (refer Figure 3.9e); or iii. have permanent screening that is a minimum 75 per cent obscure to any part of the window or active habitable below 1.6m above floor level (refer Figure 3.9f).

exceptions.label: C3.9.6 source of overlooking screened (fixed element, obscure glazing or 75% screen below 1.6 m)

replaces.note: Part C C3.10.5-C3.10.6; Table 3.9a distances relaxed (C4P1-129)

notes: from: ch3 C3.10.5-r3 (renumbered C3.9.5, exception C3.9.6). Vacant residential-zoned or unknown adjoining site: the Table 3.9a radius (6.0 m) is measured to the lot boundary. privacy.screened_or_offset also admits the C3.9.3 offset, which C3.9.6 does not list.

verified.note: C3.9.6(iii) printed 'active habitable below 1.6m' (word 'space' missing); kept as printed. The C3.9.6 exception keeps its own verify flag: privacy.screened_or_offset also admits the C3.9.3 offset, which C3.9.6 does not list, and C3.9.6's 'behind the street setback' qualifier is not tested.
